facts.icd10_text: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter

statements.text: Back pain began 09/01/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 2 weeks before this visit.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/07/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Admitted 09/11/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 8/10 despite IV analgesia.
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.
Reports back pain for about six months.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/07/2026
Patient: Delilah Wisozk, 86-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/07/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L3 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracolumbar spine.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician.
